scope.applies_to: the frozen C0 rasterizer on the EPIC-05 A100 (GPU 3, A100-SXM4-80GB, driver 592.01, CUDA 13.1, torch 2.9.1+cu128) under the real room/bicycle 16K workload, measured by the isolated inner-loop evaluator (S_eval) protocol cell = (room|bicycle) x (exp2 forward | exp backward).
scope.explicitly_NOT_generalized_to: other GPUs / architectures (Hopper/Ada/Blackwell, or different MUFU:HBM ratios), other 3DGS backends or tile sizes, or other workloads (higher live-lane population, different memory bandwidth, half-precision paths). This is a frozen-C0/A100 workload conclusion only.
scope.reason_for_scope_limit: the performance kill mechanism (memory-bandwidth-bound proxy, exp fully hidden) and the numerical kill mechanism (leader-anchored chain under/overflow on footprint-edge rows) are both specific to this backend + GPU + workload; a different backend that fuses exp with a memory op, a higher-population workload, or a GPU with a different MUFU:HBM ratio is out of scope for this campaign.

final_evidence.why_valid: Measured on the corrected contiguous trace with a SASS-certified QSCAN. Every variant is at/below 1.0 (slightly slower than DIRECT) — the scan/shuffle overhead on top of an unchanging memory roof.

final_evidence.name: raw no-guard numerical failure
final_evidence.mechanism: leader-anchored recurrence on real footprint-edge rows: when a 16-px row clips the footprint, q(xs) and q(xs+15) differ by thousands; the leader anchor G0=exp(-q(xs)) underflows to 0 while r0=exp(-d0) overflows to inf within the same subgroup -> 0*inf = NaN; FTZ-ed intermediate prefixes give finite-but-wrong values. Repair requires the per-lane direct value = exactly the P18-P0 defect mode (per-lane recompute) that invalidated the original run. The partially-live records (pop<16: 67%/79% of records) are precisely the affected class.

defects: evaluator used a position-dependent per-lane exp (the forbidden defect mode), so it could not show speedup even if the idea worked
per-lane gd=direct_G(...) recompute for the guard + guard fallback gq=gd = DIRECT work hidden in the QSCAN path
wrong first-difference formula d0=b+2a*x0 (correct a(2x0+1)+b) on a synthetic x=lane layout
trace was Gaussian-footprint uniform sampling, not real contiguous subgroups

kill_mechanisms.name: Performance: no exp-elimination headroom in the frozen C0/A100 proxy
kill_mechanisms.statement: The exp-free, SASS-certified control kernel (identical loads/store, 0 exps) runs at 1.0017x the DIRECT time (median over 4 cells). The proxy is memory-bandwidth-bound (~85% of A100 HBM peak; 1.38 GB in 0.80 ms); the per-pixel exp is ~28 us of MUFU work against an 800 us kernel and is fully hidden. No exp-elimination technique of any kind can exceed ~1.0x in this proxy. QSCAN's measured 0.9831/0.9853/0.9882 medians are simply its scan/shuffle overhead on top of an unchanging memory roof.

kill_mechanisms.name: Numerical: leader-anchored recurrence is unusable on real footprint-edge rows
kill_mechanisms.statement: On the real contiguous trace, the legal QSCAN chain (allowed exps only, pure-multiply k^j, multiplicative scan, no guard) produces NaN on 0.02%-6.8% of items, finite-but-wrong values up to |error|=0.88, and cull-branch flips on up to 4.2% of items (sub16), all far from the 1/255 threshold. Root cause: when a 16-px row clips the footprint edge, q spans thousands within the subgroup, so G0 underflows to 0 while r0 overflows to inf -> 0*inf = NaN; FTZ prefixes give finite-but-wrong values. Repairing it requires the per-lane direct value = exactly the P18-P0 defect mode (per-lane recompute) that invalidated the original run.
